text:
Detroit arrives winless in five (0-5-0), outscored 18-9, after Saturday's 5-4 loss at FLA, where the Panthers came back from three goals down. The chances say the slump is real: the Red Wings have taken 42% of the expected goals (the quality of shots) in those games. Dylan Larkin and Albert Johansson are out. Tampa Bay is 4-1-0 in its last five, outscoring teams 22-12, after a 3-1 win at CBJ, but Brayden Point is on injured reserve. Detroit lost to Tampa Bay 4-2 on Nov 3.

The teams look closer on paper than the standings suggest. At five on five, DET has taken 51% of the expected goals in its games and TBL 55%. The Lightning's power play and penalty kill both grade out better by our numbers, and our model projects 3.24 goals for TBL against 2.78 for DET. In net, projected starter Daniil Tarasov is +6.6 goals saved above expected (how many more goals a goalie stops than an average one would on the same shots) this season, while Andrei Vasilevskiy is at -0.06, though he was +23.15 last year.

Brandon Hagel has taken Point's spot beside Jake Guentzel and Nikita Kucherov and has goals in three straight (five in all). We give him a 42% shot at a goal. For Detroit, Viktor Arvidsson is pointless in five on 4.1 expected goals. Andrew Copp plays his 800th game and has stepped up to 19:48 a night with Larkin out.
